title: Orchestration scrimmage: rapid response and root-cause hunt for Dedicated pool capacity shortfall
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: On 2025-11-03 at ~09:12 UTC a subset of Dedicated customer pools started experiencing sustained throughput shortfalls and elevated request queueing. Symptoms: p95 token latency rose from baseline 180ms to >900ms for affected pools, request queues lengthened, and the autoscaler did not replenish GPU headroom fast enough. This ticket coordinates the emergency mitigations, the technical investigation, and the post-incident action items for long-term resilience.

Scope: Affected ~12 Dedicated pools across US-EAST-1 running professional-tier workload profiles (seq_len 1024, steady traffic). Not a complete fleet outage but customer-facing SLA degradation for ~6 paying customers. No data exfiltration or security breach suspected.

Priority: P0 (SLA impact, customer-facing).

Goals: 1) restore headroom and firm throughput guarantees to affected pools; 2) identify and fix the regression in scaling behavior; 3) implement guardrails to prevent recurrence and improve detection time.
acceptance_criteria: Affected pools return to baseline throughput and p95 latency < 250ms for steady-state traffic
Autoscaler consistently brings headroom to configured margin within target scale-up window (90s) for synthetic load tests
New runbook steps and two automated guardrails merged and deployed to runtime-1.22 by 2025-11-17
Postmortem with RCA and prioritized action items published and linked in this ticket
timeline: 2025-11-03 09:12 UTC: Alert fired for 'dedicated_pool_queue_depth' > 300 for pool-ods-7
2025-11-03 09:18 UTC: Automatic mitigation attempted (burst-steal to warm spare pools) but capacity reclaim was delayed by 4m due to reshard debounce bug
2025-11-03 09:27 UTC: Emergency throttle applied on affected routes to preserve latency for legacy-tier customers
2025-11-03 10:05 UTC: Manual headroom allocation from reserve cluster completed, throughput stabilized for 9/12 pools
2025-11-04: Started root-cause investigation; snapshot of autoscaler logs, kernel-selection telemetry, and orchestration events collected
steps_taken: Immediate: elevated incident to command-and-control, paged on-call Dedicated infra, and opened a cross-functional war room (ENG/PM/Support)
Mitigation: increased min_pool_size for affected pools to prevent further scale-to-zero races
Mitigation: disabled the recent scheduler change (kernel-sel v1.7.4 toggle) as a precautionary rollback
Mitigation: temporarily raised autoscaler aggressiveness for scale-up (scale_up_multiplier 1.6 -> 2.2) to reduce time-to-headroom
Mitigation: applied targeted throttles to non-critical routes to protect customer SLAs while full capacity restored
Data capture: collected continuous KV cache hit/miss metrics, request size histograms, and per-shard allocation events for 72h window
investigation_findings: Primary contributing factor: a regression in the autoscaler debounce logic that delayed scale-up when reshard events coincided with short-lived traffic spikes. The debounce timer was extended unintentionally in runtime-1.22 tuning changes.
Secondary factor: kernel-selection change (v1.7.4) increased per-instance memory pressure for long-sequence requests, reducing effective headroom per GPU by ~12% under worst-case workloads.

Tertiary factor: lack of a tight guardrail on 'effective_headroom' signal in fleet-controller; autoscaler made decisions from raw 'desired_instances' without factoring in per-instance capacity variance due to kernel memory pressure.
Monitoring gap: no single alert combined 'queue_depth' AND 'effective_headroom' drift; early signal existed but was noisy and suppressed by a suppression rule added in Aug 2025.
remediation_plan: Short-term (hotfixes): revert kernel-selection toggle for affected node image; push autoscaler debounce patch to runtime-1.22-hotfix.1
Short-term: add immediate guardrail in fleet-controller to enforce min_effective_headroom_ratio=0.75 before permitting downsizing
Medium-term: rework autoscaler to use smoothed 'effective_capacity' metric that fuses kernel memory pressure, KV cache utilization, and historical per-instance throughput
Medium-term: implement 'synthetic canary' traffic tests that run in parallel on every pool after releases touching scheduling or kernel selection
Long-term: add capacity-based SLAs and a capacity hedging policy for high-SLA customers that maintains reserved warm instances during platform updates

ENG-890125 (owner: Daniel Kim) - Kernel memory pressure metrics: instrument per-kernel resident set and publish to capacity dashboard - due 2025-11-14
ENG-890126 (owner: Sofia Liu) - Fleet-controller guardrail: enforce min_effective_headroom_ratio with alert and automated rollback policy - due 2025-11-17
ENG-890127 (owner: Miguel Torres) - Synthetic canary harness: create test harness and integrate into CI for runtime images - due 2025-12-01
ENG-890128 (owner: Support - L1) - Customer communications: send incident summary & SLA credit assessment to affected customers - due 2025-11-10
ENG-890129 (owner: Observability team) - Composite alert: 'headroom+queue drift' with low false positive tuning - due 2025-11-21
risks_and_open_questions: Risk: reverting kernel-selection may temporarily increase token cost per request for certain model variants; need cost/quality trade-off review
Open Q: Did any periodic batch jobs coincide with the spike and worsen the headroom calculation? (investigating cron history)
Open Q: Are other regions using the same scheduler default? (audit across regions required)
Risk: changing autoscaler aggressiveness could cause transient overshoot and unnecessary instance churn — need bounded implementation and safety caps
